title: Bittensor Daily News — November 4, 2026
summary: SubConnect estimates $70M in annualized subnet revenue, drawing a response from Barry Silbert. SN4 Targon shows $1.159M in trailing 30-day platform revenue, SN64 Chutes lists DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and Talisman announces access to mapped-address TAO balances. Earlier verified stories remain below.

ecosystem.headline: SubConnect estimates $70M annualized subnet revenue; Barry Silbert highlights the growth
ecosystem.summary: On November 4, SubConnect raised its estimate of annualized revenue across revenue-generating Bittensor subnets to $70M, from $50M a month earlier and $35M two months earlier. That is 40% growth in the latest monthly comparison and a doubling across two months. Its graphic dates the snapshots September 1, October 1 and November 1. At 7:44 AM Eastern, Barry Silbert quoted the report and highlighted the 40% growth. This measures an estimated annualized run rate, not $70M already earned, audited ecosystem accounts or profit. SubConnect explicitly says sustaining growth, margins and reduced emission dependence remain the test. Its $100M-plus year-end figure is an expectation, not a completed milestone.

sources.label: SubConnect original estimate and November revenue-index graphic
Barry Silbert’s November 4 response to the revenue index

ecosystem.ratingReason: A material, quantified operating-revenue estimate with dated comparisons; Silbert’s reaction adds context, not independent financial verification.

ecosystem.headline: Talisman announces detection and withdrawal of TAO at mapped EVM addresses
ecosystem.summary: On November 4, Talisman explained the distinction between ordinary EVM-key accounts and truncated 0x addresses mapped from native Bittensor accounts. Its follow-up says the wallet now detects TAO balances at those mapped addresses, displays them in the portfolio and offers withdrawal to the native account. This addresses balances that can be difficult to locate after bridges, contract payouts or transfers. The capability is a primary vendor announcement; this review did not connect a wallet, inspect private balances or execute a withdrawal. It is not an announcement that every 0x account is controlled by the same native key.

sources.label: Talisman November 4 explanation of mapped Bittensor EVM addresses
Talisman announcement of balance detection and native-account withdrawal

ecosystem.ratingReason: A practical wallet capability for accessing otherwise hard-to-find TAO; vendor attribution and untested execution are explicit.

ecosystem.headline: Security patch merges into release-487; mainnet activation is separate
ecosystem.summary: On November 3, Subtensor PR3299 merged into release-487. It tightens delayed-proxy authorization and basket-dividend minting against stale permissions and short-lived price manipulation. This is a verified code merge, not proof of a mainnet upgrade: today’s finalized review used runtime 486. No exploitation or user losses were established in this review.

sources.label: Merged security patch, November 3

ecosystem.ratingReason: A substantive protocol-security fix with a verified merge; its release-branch scope and unverified activation are explicit.

ecosystem.headline: Gamma service-credit proposal remains open
ecosystem.summary: PR3300, opened November 2 and still open at this review, proposes dollar-valued service credits minted by burning subnet alpha. The credits would be non-transferable and non-redeemable, used for a subnet’s service through a hotkey-keyed deposit. Its launch sequence requires an upgrade and enabling steps. It is not a live payment system or an observed transaction burn.

ecosystem.ratingReason: A useful protocol design to follow; code under review is not an activated capability.

ecosystem.headline: Const argues for protocol-coordinated compute across jurisdictions
ecosystem.summary: Commentary dated November 4 at 8:12 AM Eastern: Const argues that protocols can coordinate decentralized inference, compute clusters and training across jurisdictions, and names SN4 Targon’s Engy, SN64 Chutes and Instant Inference in that thesis. The post responds to Elon Musk’s remark about data centers in space. This is a view on infrastructure coordination and political concentration, not a new product launch, proof that jurisdictional risk disappears or a partnership announcement.

updates.headline: SN4 Targon’s dashboard shows $1.159M in trailing 30-day platform revenue
updates.summary: SN4 Targon’s public revenue dashboard, checked November 4, shows $1,158,560 of combined platform revenue over the trailing 30 days, alongside 15,910 total users and 8,183 new workloads in that period. The chart separates VM, Contracts, BM and Sandboxes. These are operator-published operating metrics, distinct from emissions, token valuation and profit. A bookmarked secondary report puts October revenue near $1.2M; this review verified the live trailing-window figure and does not substitute it for a reconstructed October calendar total. The dashboard’s network snapshot is dated November 4 at 17:03 UTC; the revenue window has its own 30-day definition.

sources.label: SN4 Targon official platform-revenue dashboard, reviewed November 4

updates.ratingReason: A directly visible seven-figure operating-revenue metric gives readers substantive commercial evidence, with the operator attribution and measurement window explicit.

updates.headline: SN37 Aurelius merges opt-in renewals with a persistent spending cap
updates.summary: PR33 merged into SN37 Aurelius’s main branch on November 4 at 03:19:52 UTC, or November 3 at 10:19:52 PM Eastern. It adds an optional helper to restage a winning entry within an explicit lifetime WT limit and per-evaluation ceiling. The design retains authorization across restarts and uncertain outcomes, stops after a loss or timeout, and waits when evidence or funding is missing. The WT budget is not a TAO-denominated spending claim. The patch does not change coldkey funding, selection or weights. This is merged implementation, not a verified live deployment or uninterrupted-reward guarantee.

sources.label: SN37 Aurelius merged renewal helper and limits

updates.ratingReason: A practical optional miner workflow with explicit authorization limits; production use and payouts were not tested.

updates.headline: SN51 Lium bounds pod edits when a container will not stop
updates.summary: SN51 Lium merged PR2048 on November 4 at 15:51:11 UTC, or 10:51:11 AM Eastern. A pod edit or reboot could hang when a remote container-stop command never returned. The patch bounds the edit-swap commands and rollback path; if stopping and killing still fail, it restores the container’s name and fails the edit while retaining its volume. The author explicitly does not claim an overall timeout for every create operation, which can include legitimate long image pulls. This is verified merged code, not an independently exercised rental or confirmed fleet-wide upgrade.

sources.label: SN51 Lium merged bounded pod-edit recovery, November 4

updates.ratingReason: A concrete rental-reliability fix with explicit limits; merge status does not establish customer execution.

updates.headline: SN64 Chutes lists DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at $0.30 input and $1.20 output
updates.summary: At 11:04 AM Eastern on November 4, SN64 Chutes announced DeepSeek V4.1 Flash availability. Its public catalog lists deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 as Hot, with prices per million tokens of $0.30 input, $1.20 output and $0.03 cached input. The same catalog lists V4 Pro at $0.85 input and $2.65 output. Developers can choose between the models through Chutes’ API rather than use the larger model for every call. Listing and advertised pricing were directly checked; authenticated inference, uptime and comparative benchmark scores were not independently tested. This is separate from the still-planned Tencent Hy4 integration.

updates.headline: SN71 Leadpoet merges recovery for completed paid Arena work
updates.summary: SN71 Leadpoet merged PR1015 on November 4 at 11:32:50 UTC. The patch keeps completed-result delivery running during shutdown, rechecks cancellation and deadlines before provider dispatch, and retains successful sanitized replies when billing persistence fails. Exact same-call retries can reuse the retained result rather than issue another provider request, while unresolved costs remain subject to normal ledger reconciliation. The PR explicitly leaves verifier prompts, judging criteria, historical outcomes and reward rules unchanged. This code merge does not establish a production rollout or resolve the separately reported baseline-verifier mismatch.

sources.label: SN71 Leadpoet merged paid-work recovery patch

updates.ratingReason: A meaningful reliability change for completed work and duplicate provider requests; deployment and the separate judging issue remain unverified.

updates.headline: SN92 REAX adds 24-hour notice for reward-rule changes
updates.summary: The SN92 REAX FAQ’s version 3.8, dated November 4 at 11:45 UTC, requires at least 24 hours’ notice for changes to tiers, shares, targets, pools or scoring. Adding an inference model is exempt, but needs a versioned release stating its pool and scoring; removing or replacing a model is not exempt. The page says already-earned amounts are not taken away. Separately, version 3.7 was decided November 2 and announced November 3: the three full-share days start at award approval, or crowning if approval came first, from the next crowning. Current champions get a one-time adjustment without double payment. These are documented rules; this review did not reconstruct individual payouts.

sources.label: SN92 REAX FAQ v3.8 and dated change log

updates.ratingReason: Concrete notice and payment-timing rules help miners understand changes; no payout or new allocation execution is inferred.

updates.headline: SN117 EveryFrame announces a film-contest treasury from unused miner allocation
updates.summary: Dated November 3, last edited 3:11 PM Eastern: SN117 EveryFrame says unused miner allocation will fund its AI Film Contest rather than be recycled. Serving fees and a 10–50% output-quality bonus are paid to miners first; the treasury receives the remainder of the miner portion, with owner and validator allocations separate. The team identifies treasury UIDs 156/157 and describes community voting and on-chain awards. Its public dashboard currently shows “Treasury data unavailable,” so this review did not verify balances, completed payouts or actual routing. The promotional split graphic is illustrative, not a fixed whole-subnet percentage. This is a team-announced funding policy, not a qualifying transaction burn or measured creator adoption.
